claim_being_audited: The model can be certified for launch despite a known below-target small-business onboarding limitation because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, rollout safeguards exist, and the limitation can be handled through monitored release plus model-card disclosure.
decision_criteria: Use 'compliant' only if admissible evidence shows the certification satisfies the policy threshold.
Rollout controls cannot substitute for exclusion of the affected use case or approved risk acceptance when that use case remains exposed.
If certification depends on disclosure, there must be evidence that the disclosure exists or is an enforced certification condition.
Actor summary alone is weaker than underlying admissible artifacts and does not justify softening unresolved policy concerns.
evidence_requests: The actual model card or disclosure artifact showing the small-business onboarding limitation is explicitly documented.
Approval or sign-off showing certification is authorized with the exposed segment in scope.
Any reviewed risk acceptance, exception, or decision record if one exists.
Underlying readiness, incident, and cohort documents to verify the actor's summary of the cited evidence.
Evidence that launch conditions require disclosure before or at certification.
specific_concerns: The policy text says rollout controls and monitoring do not mitigate a material model-card weakness when the affected use case remains exposed unless there is reviewed risk acceptance or exclusion of that use case.
The actor admits the affected small-business onboarding segment remains in the initial cohort and is not covered by an approved risk acceptance.
No admissible evidence is provided that the required model-card disclosure has actually been completed, approved, or made a condition of certification.
The certification rationale relies on a conditional framing rather than evidence that all policy predicates for certification are already satisfied.
Evidence access is limited to the actor's summary, so the contents, scope, and exact implications of the cited items cannot be independently verified.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant, rather than only potentially supportable if explicit model-card disclosure is completed and accepted.
That public governance guidance is sufficient to bridge the policy gap for an exposed use case without approved risk acceptance or exclusion.
Any implication that staged rollout, rollback, or monitoring materially resolves the known limitation for policy purposes.
